title: What is known about 1RB1LA_1RC1RD_0LA0LD_1RE1LC_0RF0LF_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_1RC1RD_0LA0LD_1RE1LC_0RF0LF_---0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A bouncer over the 5-cell word 11100 grows to the right; the slow left side is a dense irregular mixture of runs of 1 to 6 ones; chaotic, open.
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone), 8 shift rules of the sweeps; the rest of the description below is observation of the run, marked as such.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: D with 0 under the head, 0 right, 0 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 24,723 cells have been visited and 15,052 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.163). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.572).

claims.title: 8 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: A, C and D cross rotations of 11100 leftward, rewriting them (e.g. D: 11100 → 01010). Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (F reading 0) needs 01110 to the left; the right side is unconstrained. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer over a 11100 background, chaotic slow side
claims.text: The right part of the tape is the word 11100 repeated (right end at step 2.7·108: 3 : 3 : 3 : … 3 : 2 . in run notation), growing like √t: a bouncer whose leftward passes rewrite each copy (eight proved shift rules) and whose rightward passes restore it.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (F reading 0) needs 01110 to the left; the right side is unconstrained. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer over a 11100 background, chaotic slow side
claims.text: The right part of the tape is the word 11100 repeated (right end at step 2.7·108: 3 : 3 : 3 : … 3 : 2 . in run notation), growing like √t: a bouncer whose leftward passes rewrite each copy (eight proved shift rules) and whose rightward passes restore it.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. F reading 0 halts. The 5-cell closed language puts 01110 to the left of the head; the right side is unconstrained (it allows blank tape after the head).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

sections.heading: What the machine does: bouncer over a 11100 background, chaotic slow side
html: The right part of the tape is the word 11100 repeated (right end at step 2.7·108: 3 : 3 : 3 : … 3 : 2 . in run notation), growing like √t: a bouncer whose leftward passes rewrite each copy (eight proved shift rules) and whose rightward passes restore it.

The left side (3,507 cells after 109 steps, exponent about 0.16) is different: runs of one to six 1s with gaps of one or two 0s and no visible order, e.g. . 3 . 1 . 1 . 1 . 1 . 1 . 1 . 1 . 2 . 1 . 1 . 1 . 1 . 2 . 1 …. Between 5.80·108 and 5.80·108+70,000 steps the left wall advances 120 cells in a burst, and only 30 more in the next 4.5·107 steps: the slow side grows in bursts.

sections.heading: What a halt would require
html: F reading 0 halts. The 5-cell closed language puts 01110 to the left of the head; the right side is unconstrained (it allows blank tape after the head).

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html:
• Sweeps (lean/Sweeps.lean, kernel): A, C and D cross rotations of 11100 leftward, rewriting them (e.g. D: 11100 → 01010); for every number of copies and every tape around.
  • Bounded run (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in 107 steps (native), 10,000 (kernel); the halting transition is the only way to stop.
Everything else on this page is observation of the simulated run (heuristic). Nothing here decides halting.

sections.heading: What would move it forward
html: Look at the boundary between the 11100 region and the chaotic region: which words cross it per pass.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.163). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.572).
After 109 steps the tape spans 24,723 cells (3,507 left of the start, 14,986 right), with a density of 1s of 0.609.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.
